decisions.reason: As a 2023 product line tightly linked to the firm’s established geospatial integration business and already presented on its own page, it likely meets at least minimum aspirations or is close enough that the firm’s slack justifies keeping it while market evidence accumulates.

The building data digital twin service is strategically attractive but more market-uncertain and implementation-heavy, so while its early signal is weaker, a medium-sized R&D-active German GeoIT firm would usually keep it for another year before reallocating resources.

Because this authentication and identity delegation service is only close rather than central to the core offer and may face slower uptake, it has a relatively higher drop risk, but its relevance for enterprise and public-sector integration still supports retention under uncertain early performance.

An open GIS application development framework fits the firm’s platform-based consulting and engineering model well, so even if short-term sales are still forming, its complementarities with services and future projects make continued support more likely than withdrawal.

The explicitly launched identity and access service for GIS applications is closely aligned with customer needs for secure integration, and given the firm’s broad portfolio and available organisational slack, management would likely keep it unless clearer underperformance emerges.
